items.title: CLI project create silently drops unreadable or malformed --metadata-json
items.body:
## Reproduction

I reproduced this on current main `93d4031572df0ab05307558eb8d8486cdc4c287c` with Node 24.18.0 and pnpm 10.33.2, using the normally built `apps/daemon/dist/cli.js`.

With a local HTTP capture server as `--daemon-url`, run:

```sh
printf '{"kind":' > invalid.json
od project create --metadata-json invalid.json --daemon-url "$DAEMON_URL" --json
od project create --metadata-json missing.json --daemon-url "$DAEMON_URL" --json
printf '{"kind":' | od project create --metadata-json - --daemon-url "$DAEMON_URL" --json
```

All three commands exit **0** and send `POST /api/projects` **without** the requested metadata. Valid object JSON from both a file and stdin is sent correctly in the positive controls. The capture server only witnesses the real compiled CLI's HTTP requests; this reproduction does not claim a provider run or persistent-project acceptance test.

An explicitly supplied metadata input that cannot be read or parsed should fail with the CLI usage/input exit code before sending a project-creation request, preserving the underlying diagnostic.

`safeReadJsonFile` catches filesystem and JSON errors and returns null; `runProject` then silently skips metadata. The previous ESM fixes #2292 / #4060 repaired valid reads but retain this catch-and-continue behavior. items.title: [Bug]: official Dockerfile ships no agent CLI — opencode/Vela login required workaround
items.body:
## Description

The official `deploy/Dockerfile` (runtime stage, `node:24-alpine`) ships **no
agent CLI at all** — neither OpenCode nor the Vela CLI is installed in the
image. On a fresh container built from this Dockerfile, any `start_run`
against the `opencode`/`byok-opencode` agent fails immediately:

```

```

requires a Vela login to populate that path.

3. Observe the `opencode binary not found` failure above — the runtime

items.title: Research CLI treats string option values before search as subcommands
items.body:
## Reproduction

Confirmed on main `93d4031572df0ab05307558eb8d8486cdc4c287c` with the built CLI, Node 24.18.0, pnpm 10.33.2. A local HTTP capture server returned a fixed JSON response without contacting Tavily.

```sh
od research search --query design --daemon-url "$DAEMON_URL"
# exit 0; POST /api/research/search with query="design"
od research --daemon-url "$DAEMON_URL" search --query design
# exit 2; unknown subcommand: od research <daemon URL>
od research --query design search --daemon-url "$DAEMON_URL"
# exit 2; unknown subcommand: od research design
od research --max-sources 3 search --query design --daemon-url "$DAEMON_URL"
# exit 2; unknown subcommand: od research 3
```

## Expected behavior

String-option values should remain values during subcommand discovery, so placing the existing options before `search` dispatches the same request as placing them after it. Preserve a literal query equal to `search`, equals-form options, help, and malformed-input rejection. This is a small CLI usability/correctness fix; no research provider, result schema, or network policy changes.

## Cause / duplicate check

`splitResearchSubcommand` selects the first argument not starting with `--` without skipping values of known string options. Its original regression only covers a verb-first query equal to `search`. The current open #4868 changes built-in research skills/prompts and does not change this CLI dispatcher or helper.

items.title: Inline HTML export misses entity-encoded asset filenames and double-escapes style attributes
items.body:
## Reproduction

Reproduced with the production `inlineRelativeAssets` implementation compiled from main `93d4031572df0ab05307558eb8d8486cdc4c287c`, real temporary asset files, and JSDOM as an independent HTML-attribute oracle. The owning HTTP surface is `GET /api/projects/:id/export/*?inline=1`.

Given existing files `theme&dark.css` and `boot&main.js`:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="theme&dark.css">
<script src="boot&main.js"></script>
```

The exporter attempts `theme&` (the undecoded numeric reference becomes a URL fragment) and `boot&main.js`, so neither asset is inlined. The same files with plain ampersands inline correctly.

A second case with a resolvable href:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="theme&dark.css" title="R&D" media="screen and (width > 500px)">
```

After inlining, the browser-visible title becomes literal `R&D` instead of `R&D`, and media contains literal `>` instead of `>`. The raw attribute value is escaped a second time.

## Expected behavior

Interpret HTML character references in attribute context before resolving local asset paths and before carrying stylesheet attributes to the generated style element. Preserve original script attributes, safe output escaping, external-URL exclusion, and the current byte/concurrency limits.

`readHtmlAttr` currently returns raw source text from a regular expression. Use the existing HTML parser dependency at this common attribute boundary; this does not require changi

items.title: fix(vscode-ide-companion): comma operator in activate() leaks two Disposables (gemini.diff.accept, onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders)
items.body:
### What happened?

In the VS Code companion extension (`packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/extension.ts`), the `activate()` function pushes its Disposables into `context.subscriptions` in two `context.subscriptions.push(...)` calls. In each call, two registrations are wrapped in an extra pair of parentheses, which turns them into a single **comma expression** instead of separate arguments:

```ts
// group 1
(vscode.commands.registerCommand('gemini.diff.accept', ...),
 vscode.commands.registerCommand('gemini.diff.cancel', ...)),

// group 2
(vscode.workspace.onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders(...),
 vscode.workspace.onDidGrantWorkspaceTrust(...)),
```

A comma expression evaluates both operands but its value is only the **last** one. So both registrations actually run (the command and listener are created), but only the second Disposable of each group (`gemini.diff.cancel`, `onDidGrantWorkspaceTrust`) is passed to `push()` and tracked in `context.subscriptions`. The `gemini.diff.accept` command Disposable and the `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders` listener Disposable are never added, so they are never disposed on deactivation.

Consequences:
- On deactivation/reload within the same extension host (e.g. an extension update), the `gemini.diff.accept` command stays registered. Re-activation then throws `command 'gemini.diff.accept' already exists`.
- The `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders` listener is never torn down, so a stale listener keeps firing `ideServer.syncEnvVars()` against an `IDEServer

items.title: Nix CLI discovery misses Home Manager's /etc/profiles/per-user/$USER/bin (follow-up to #6121)
items.body:
## Before you submit

- [x] I searched existing issues and confirmed this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I replaced the example text with the real behavior, reproduction steps, expected result, and version from the app's About menu or `od --version`.

## What happened?

Follow-up to #6121 (fixed by #6885). That issue covered nix-darwin `environment.systemPackages` → `/run/current-system/sw/bin`, and the fix added three Nix directories to the shared toolchain resolver. One standard Nix location was missed:

**`/etc/profiles/per-user/$USER/bin`** — where packages land when **Home Manager runs as a nix-darwin (or NixOS) module**, which is the dominant way Home Manager is deployed.

So Nix users are still split by install shape:

| Install shape | Binary lands in | Detected in 0.21.1 |
|---|---|---|
| nix-darwin `environment.systemPackages` | `/run/current-system/sw/bin` | ✅ (via #6885) |
| standalone `nix profile install` | `~/.nix-profile/bin` | ✅ (via #6885) |
| Determinate/default profile | `/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin` | ✅ (via #6885) |
| **Home Manager as a nix-darwin/NixOS module** | **`/etc/profiles/per-user/$USER/bin`** | ❌ |

Verified against the shipped 0.21.1 bundle — `wellKnownUserToolchainBins` in `Open Design.app/Contents/Resources/app/prebundled/packaged-main.mjs` contains the three dirs above, and `grep -c "etc/profiles"` over that file returns `0`.

items.title: [Bug]: Updating a user design system prepends a second "# Title" before the DESIGN.md frontmatter
items.body:
### Before you submit

- [x] I searched existing issues and confirmed this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I replaced the example text with the real behavior, reproduction steps, expected result, and version from the app's About menu or `od --version`.

### What happened?

Updating a user design system without a new body (for example toggling Published, or editing its metadata) writes a second `# <title>` line at the very top of `DESIGN.md`, before the YAML frontmatter:

```
# Cubbit

---
name: "Cubbit"
...
---

# Cubbit
```

The file then no longer starts with `---`, so it is not a valid frontmatter document anymore. For a design system installed from git, it is also a local change that blocks the next `git pull` of the package.

The cause is in [`withDesignSystemHeader`](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/blob/7abd6fc2b11987c3940eb4ffc461478ff37c0b33/apps/daemon/src/design-systems/index.ts#L3447), called from [`updateUserDesignSystem`](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/blob/7abd6fc2b11987c3940eb4ffc461478ff37c0b33/apps/daemon/src/design-systems/index.ts#L1357):

```ts
let next = body.replace(/^#\s+.*$/m, `# ${input.title}`);
if (next === body && !/^#\s+/.test(next)) next = `# ${input.title}\n\n${next}`;
```

When the existing H1 already equals the title, the replace is a no-op, so `next === body`. The second check has no `m` flag, so it only looks at the first line (`---`) and prepends a new heading.

1. Install a design system whose `DESIGN.md` s

items.title: New Project dialog unreachable since #6142 — no way to bind a project to a local working directory
items.body:
## Summary

Since #6142 ("the #5517 redesign", `356c8c364`, 2026-08-05) a signed-out install has **no reachable entry to the New Project dialog**. That dialog is the only surface in the product that binds a project to a local working directory, so users cannot create a project whose generated files land in their own folder — everything goes to the managed project store and stays invisible to their git.

Affects every release from **v0.18.0** (2026-08-06) through **v0.22.2** and current `main`. **v0.17.0** (2026-08-03) is the last good version.

## Why this matters

There are two folder pickers with opposite semantics:

| Surface | Writes | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Home composer / `+` composer menu ("Working directory") | `metadata.linkedDirs` | read-only `--add-dir` awareness; artifacts still go to the managed store |
| New Project dialog, folder button next to the name field | `metadata.baseDir` (via `POST /api/projects/:id/working-dir`) | OD works **inside** the user's folder |

Only the second one makes generated work land in a git-tracked directory. Users find the first one (it is on the home screen, labelled "Working directory"), reasonably assume it is the working directory, and then discover their files are not in their repo. The dialog that would do what they want cannot be opened at all.

items.body: ### What happened? I'm running Gemini CLI locally on arch linux with the podman sandbox enabled: `GEMINI_SANDBOX=podman` When i run npm start, the CLI gets to the point where it rebuilds one of the native dependencies inside the sandbox, but the rebuild fails, i've attached the full output below. This seems to be related to how the sandbox handles UID/GID mapping with rootless podman. From what I understand, the current flow creates a user inside the container with the same UID/GID as the host user and then runs Gemini as that user. That works when the container UID maps directly to the host UID, but rootless Podman normally uses a user namespace, so that's not necessarily the case. Because the project is bind-mounted into the container, this can result in files being owned by a UID that the host user can't modify. In my case, that eventually shows up as `node-gyp` being unable to remove the `build` directory. ### What did you expect to happen? If the sandbox is using rootless podman and UID/GID mapping is enabled, I would expect the CLI to handle the user namespace mapping automatically so that bind-mounted files remain owned by host user. something like `podman run --userns=keep-id` should be added automatically for rootless podman, unless the user has already supplied their own --userns option through `SANDBOX_FLAGS`. items.body:
## What happened?

The web app crashes on **every page load** with an uncaught syntax error, so the UI never renders (white screen / Next.js error overlay):

```
Uncaught SyntaxError: '' literal not terminated before end of script
    at (app-pages-browser)/./src/hooks/useProjectRunStatuses.ts (…SettingsDia-16f400.js:11103:1)
    at … EntryNavRail.tsx → EntryShell.tsx → EntryView.tsx → App.tsx → ClientApp → Page
```

The stack is always the same, it is deterministic (not a flaky dev-server race), and it survives a full `tools-dev` restart.

## Root cause

`apps/web/src/hooks/useProjectRunStatuses.ts` contains **raw NUL bytes (`0x00`)** inside string literals, where the escape `\u0000` should be. The byte `0x00` is committed directly into the source (GitHub serves the file as `application/octet-stream` because of it):

```ts
const idsKey = useMemo(() => [...projectIds].sort().join('<0x00>'), [projectIds]);   // line 238
...
const subscription: Subscription = { ids: idsKey.split('<0x00>'), contextRef };      // line 245
...
for (const projectId of idsKey.split('<0x00>')) {                                     // line 253
```

(`<0x00>` = a literal NUL byte, not text.)

Modern Chromium/V8 rejects a raw control byte inside a string literal as an unterminated string, which produces `'' literal not terminated before end of script`. Node's older V8 (e.g. Node 24, V8 13.6) tolerates it, which is why this only surfaces in the browser.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Check out `main` at `1b4

items.title: [Bug]: Plugin-details views appear as workspace tabs alongside projects and pile up as identical "插件详情" entries
items.body:
**EN summary**: In the workspace top bar, the tab dropdown next to the project name lists plugin-details views as siblings of project tabs. Every run that applies a plugin opens another tab titled with the generic string “插件详情” (plugin details) — no plugin name, no dedupe, no way to close them — so the dropdown fills up with indistinguishable entries. Design expectation: **this entry point should only show concrete projects**; plugin-details should not be a workspace-level tab at all.

## 环境

- Open Design **0.24.1**（stable），macOS 27.0 (26A428)，Apple Silicon；web bundle 为 `open-design-web-standalone`（Next.js）
- 项目内多次运行（run）后出现，持续累积、重启不清除

## 现象

项目名旁的下拉菜单（workspace tabs dropdown）里出现 **5 个一模一样的「插件详情」**（grid 图标），与当前项目并列展示，无法区分、无法清理：

- 数据库证据完全对应：该项目的 `applied_plugin_snapshots` 表正好 5 行 —— `example-web-prototype` ×1、`od-next-strategy` ×2（09-21 两次 run）、`design-system-ant` ×2（09-24 两次 run）。**每次 run 应用插件都会新开一个插件详情标签**，5 次 → 5 个标签。

## 代码层根因（0.24.1 发货 chunk，标识符经压缩）

1. **大一统标签模型**：`marketplace` 类标签（含带 `pluginId` 的插件详情）与 `project` 标签存放在同一个 tabs 数组；下拉菜单渲染 `tabs.filter(kind !== "entry")` 并按最近使用排序——插件详情视图被当成与项目同级的标签列出；
2. **标题写死**：标签标题映射为 `t(pluginId ? "workspaceTabs.pluginDetails" : "workspaceTabs.marketplace")`，**从不显示插件名**，N 个标签全部显示为「插件详情」；
3. **不去重、不可关闭**：每次打开都生成全新 id（`` `marketplace:${pluginId ?? "index"}:${uid}` ``），代码中唯一的去重逻辑只针对 `"entry"` 类标签，插件类标签只增不减。

## 设计期望（本 issue 的核心反馈）

**这个入口应该只是具体项目的展示与切换（project-only）。** 插件详情是从插件市场 / 运行流程派生的临时视图，不是工作区实体，不应作为 workspace 级标签与项目并列展示。

若产品上确实需

items.title: Feature Request: Option to make laser drawings persistent (like iPad laser)
items.body:
### Feature Request: Option to make laser drawings persistent (like iPad laser)

**Description**  
Right now, when using the laser tool, the drawn line disappears automatically after a few seconds.  
It would be useful to have an **option to keep the laser visible until manually cleared or toggled off**.  

This would mimic the behavior of the iPad’s laser pointer, where users can choose between a temporary (disappearing) laser and a persistent one.

---

**Why this is useful**  
- Allows presenters to highlight something for a longer time without it fading too quickly.  
- Gives users control over whether the laser is **temporary** (current behavior) or **persistent** (proposed option).  
- Makes it easier in teaching, demos, and collaborative sessions where emphasis needs to stay visible.  

---

**Suggested approach**  
- Add a toggle/checkbox in the laser tool menu:  
  - *Temporary (default)* → laser disappears after a few seconds.  
  - *Persistent* → laser remains on the canvas until disabled or cleared.  
- Keep current behavior as default for backward compatibility.

---

**Example**  
- Select laser tool → draw line → it stays visible until manually cleared.  
- Toggle back to temporary mode → laser fades after a few seconds (same as now).

items.title: [Bug]: Packaged Electron disk cache grows unbounded during task previews (SimpleCache / critique max-age=3600)
items.body:
Related to #8282 / #8283. The token-gap PR stops `ERR_NO_BUFFER_SPACE` from being amplified through undici. This issue is the likely **source** of the kernel-buffer exhaustion: Chromium SimpleCache in the Helper writing large HTTP responses with no packaged disk-cache cap.

### Before you submit

- [x] I searched existing issues and confirmed this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I replaced the example text with the real behavior, reproduction steps, expected result, and version from the app's About menu or `od --version`.

### What happened?

On packaged Open Design 0.22.2 (`release-stable-intel`), a Helper disk-writes diagnostic recorded **2147.49 MB in 954 s** of `pwrite`/`ftruncate` inside Electron Framework. Maintainer analysis on #8282 attributes that pattern to Chromium SimpleCache (network-service HTTP disk cache), not app-level TypeScript writes.

After the last reboot, the live cache is still large:

- Path (namespaced, not the generic `~/Library/Application Support/Open Design/Cache`):
  `~/Library/Application Support/Open Design/namespaces/release-stable-intel/user-data/session/Cache/Cache_Data`
- Size: **407 MB**, **2025** files
- Largest entries are 7–10 MB (`*_s` / `todelete_*_s_*`), several written again at 11:14–11:20 local after the 10:41 reboot

Most daemon routes send `Cache-Control: no-store` / `no-cache`. Critique artifacts do not — `apps/daemon/src/critique/artifact-handler.ts` sets `Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600` for content-addressed HTML/SVG that can

items.title: Reasonix connection test persists a probe session into the user's Reasonix state home
items.body:
## What happens

1. An agent connection test for the Reasonix CLI runs `reasonix acp` inside a throwaway `od-conn-test-*` temp dir (`apps/daemon/src/connectionTest.ts`), with `cwd` pointed at the temp dir.
2. The probe sends a real smoke prompt, so the Reasonix CLI starts an actual session — and persists it into the user's **real state home** (`%APPDATA%\reasonix\sessions\*.jsonl`), because the test isolates `cwd` but not the child's state root.
3. Reasonix's session import then picks that file up; since the probe's cwd belongs to no project, the conversation gets bound to the default workspace.

Net effect: every "Test connection" click deposits a ghost conversation into the user's Reasonix app — one the user never created and can't attribute to OpenDesign.

## Proposed fix

One line in `connectionTest.ts`: set `REASONIX_STATE_HOME=<tempDir>` in the env handed to the reasonix probe.

Per Reasonix's documented path model (its `docs/CONFIG_PATHS.md`), `REASONIX_STATE_HOME` relocates state (sessions/archive/memory) only; `config.toml` and `.env` provider credentials stay under `REASONIX_HOME`, which the daemon already sets — so auth and the smoke result are unchanged. The temp dir is already removed in the `finally` block, so probe sessions vanish with it.

A regression test (red without the fix, green with) is ready; PR to follow.

items.title: fix(media): send image_urls to Fal Seedream edit endpoints
items.body:
﻿## Summary

Fal image-to-image requests fail for `fal-ai/bytedance/seedream/v4/edit` because Open Design sends the reference image as singular `image_url`. The Seedream edit endpoint requires an `image_urls` array.

## Environment

- Open Design packaged app on Windows x64
- Provider: Fal.ai (BYOK)
- Model endpoint: `fal-ai/bytedance/seedream/v4/edit`
- Invocation path: `media generate`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a working Fal.ai API key in Open Design.
2. Put a reference image in the project directory.
3. Run:

```powershell
& $env:OD_NODE_BIN $env:OD_BIN media generate `
  --surface image `
  --model 'fal-ai/bytedance/seedream/v4/edit' `
  --prompt 'Create a refined variation of this reference image.' `
  --image 'reference.jpg' `
  --output 'seedream-edit.png' `
  --workspace $env:OD_WORKSPACE_ID `
  --workspace-member $env:OD_WORKSPACE_MEMBER_ID
```

4. Fal accepts the queued request, but the generation fails with HTTP 422 because `image_urls` is missing.

This produces a payload shaped like:

```json
{
  "prompt": "...",
  "image_url": "data:image/jpeg;base64,..."
}
```

That shape works for Fal models that accept singular `image_url`, but Seedream's edit endpoint rejects it.

Open Design should send Seedream edit references using the endpo

items.body:
## Summary

The Home page can show a horizontal scrollbar at the bottom even though the page content already fits within the viewport.

## Current behavior

On Home, a bottom horizontal scrollbar appears and can be dragged left/right, but the visible page content is already fully displayed. There is no meaningful overflow for the user to inspect, so the scrollbar feels spurious.

## Expected behavior

Home should not expose a horizontal scrollbar when the page content fits inside the available width. If nothing is actually overflowing, the page should remain horizontally locked.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Home page.
2. Observe the bottom edge of the window.
3. Notice that a horizontal scrollbar is present.
4. Drag it left/right and observe that the page content is already fully visible and does not need horizontal scrolling.

## Notes

This looks like an overflow/layout regression rather than intentional behavior. Likely causes include:

- a child container exceeding viewport width by a few pixels
- mixed width calculations between the Home layout and fixed/sticky surfaces
- padding/gap/border math causing the root scroller to think it overflows horizontally

A user recording is available and shows the unnecessary bottom scrollbar on Home.

## Why this matters

Unnecessary horizontal scrollbars make the page feel unstable and visually unpolished, especially on a landing surface like Home where the layout otherwise appears to fit cleanly.

items.title: Three max-tokens defaults exceed MAX_MAX_TOKENS and cannot be restored after an override
items.body:
### What happens

`apps/web/src/state/maxTokens.ts` defines both the validation bound and defaults that exceed it:

- `MIN_MAX_TOKENS = 1024`, `MAX_MAX_TOKENS = 200000`
- defaults above that bound: `deepseek-v4-pro: 384000`, `deepseek-v4-flash: 384000`, `qwen3-coder:480b: 262144`

`effectiveMaxTokens` returns the user's override when `isValidOverride` accepts it, otherwise the model default, and the Settings field validates against the same bounds. So for these three models the shipped default is used for provider requests, while the same number cannot be typed into the control that displays it as its placeholder.

The consequence is one-directional. A user on `deepseek-v4-pro` who edits Max tokens once cannot get back to the shipped 384000 through the UI — the field rejects it. Clearing the field does restore the default, so the value is reachable only by not setting one, which is not something the control suggests.

Noted by @lefarcen in #7995: "a larger shipped default can therefore be used automatically but cannot be entered again through the same control."

Found while discussing Cloud model discovery in #7995. It predates that work and is independent of it — discovery should not change output-cap behaviour — so it is split out to keep that issue's acceptance criteria reviewable.

items.title: Document Docker build resource requirements when GHCR image is not pullable
items.body:
## Summary

The documented Docker self-hosting path currently points users at the prebuilt GHCR image:

```bash
OPEN_DESIGN_IMAGE=ghcr.io/nexu-io/od:latest docker compose pull
OPEN_DESIGN_IMAGE=ghcr.io/nexu-io/od:latest docker compose up -d --no-build
```

But `ghcr.io/nexu-io/od` is not publicly pullable today, so users are forced into local source builds. The docs do not currently warn that local Docker builds need substantially more memory/CPU than the final runtime container.

This creates a second failure mode for small self-hosting VPS users: after the public image pull fails with `unauthorized`, a local build can fail or hang during the Next.js production build step on small droplets.

## What happened

On a fresh small DigitalOcean Ubuntu 24.04 droplet, the documented prebuilt image path fails:

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/nexu-io/od:latest
# Error response from daemon: error from registry: unauthorized
# unauthorized
```

The same result was reproduced with specific tags:

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/nexu-io/od:0.14.1
# unauthorized

docker pull ghcr.io/nexu-io/od:0.14.0
# unauthorized

docker pull ghcr.io/nexu-io/od:0.13.0
# unauthorized

docker pull ghcr.io/nexu-io/od:0.12.0
# unauthorized
```

When falling back to a local Docker build, the build reaches this step:

```text
RUN pnpm --filter @open-design/daemon build && \
    pnpm --filter @open-design/web build && \
    pnpm --filter @open-design/daemon deploy --legacy --prod /app/deploy/daemon ...

> @open-design

items.title: [Bug]: MCP server instructions are 5,859 chars — Claude Code truncates at 2,048, discarding all run-commissioning guidance
items.body:
### Before you submit
- [x] I searched existing issues and confirmed this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I replaced the example text with the real behavior, reproduction steps, expected result, and version.

### What happened?

`od mcp`'s MCP `instructions` field is **5,859 characters**. Claude Code truncates MCP server instructions at **2,048 characters** — a documented, intended per-server cap — so **3,811 characters (65%) never reach the model**.

The cut lands mid-sentence, immediately before the run-commissioning section:

```
...explicitly without making any other tool call.

To make Open        <-- truncated here
```

Everything after that point is discarded. That is the entire "how to actually drive Open Design" half:

| guidance | reaches the model? |
|---|---|
| read-only tools (`get_artifact`, `get_file`, `search_files`, `list_files`) | yes |
| `list_skills` / `list_plugins` — *"you do not run skills yourself"* | **no** |
| `list_agents` before `start_run.agent` — *"do not guess"* | **no** |
| `collect_brief` / `confirm_brief` | **no** |
| `start_run(..., requestId, ...)` idempotency contract | **no** |
| `failureAction:"recharge"` / `resume:true` | **no** |
